How confidence is setIt follows the kind of evidence, not judgement.
  • The customer's own statement (high confidence at most): The organisation says so itself: its press release, website, annual report or a named executive on the record.
  • Regulatory or securities filing (high confidence at most): A filing by the customer or the vendor names the relationship.
  • Independent press (high confidence at most): Editorially independent reporting describes the deployment.
  • Joint announcement (medium confidence at most): A press release issued with the vendor, usually with a quote from the customer.
  • Vendor case study (medium confidence at most): The vendor's published customer story naming the organisation.
  • Vendor mention only (low confidence at most): A logo, a customer list or a passing mention by the vendor, with nothing from the customer.
  • An organisation that also holds a stake in the vendor is labelled “Investor and customer” and is never rated above medium.
  • A partnership is listed as a partner, not a customer.

Reputation

Adverse items are attributed to their sources and need one primary source or two independent ones before they are published.

Reputation
Regulatory actionsNo public evidence Ask the vendor: Has Versa Networks been the subject of any regulatory investigation or enforcement action?
LitigationNo public evidence Ask the vendor: Is Versa Networks party to any material litigation, pending or resolved in the last three years?
Security incidentsAccording to Versa's security bulletin published on 2024-08-26, CVE-2024-39717, a high-severity file-upload flaw in Versa Director, was exploited at least once by an advanced persistent threat actor against managed service providers whose management ports were reachable from the internet. Versa stated that a hot fix was issued on 2024-06-21, that version 22.1.4 is not affected, and that the flaw was added to the US CISA catalogue of known exploited vulnerabilities. Questions to ask the vendor (10)

  1. In what year was Versa Networks founded?
    Company age is an input to maturity and viability.
  2. How many people does Versa Networks employ, and how many are in support and engineering?
    Headcount indicates capacity to support large customers.
  3. What was Versa Networks' revenue in its last fiscal year, and is it audited?
    Revenue is the main public measure of a private vendor's scale.
  4. How many customers does Versa Networks have, and how many are banks?
    A customer count shows adoption.
  5. Has Versa Networks made any workforce reductions in the last three years?
    Layoffs can signal financial stress or reduced support capacity.
  6. Has Versa Networks been the subject of any regulatory investigation or enforcement action?
    Enforcement history bears on a supplier's conduct risk.
  7. Is Versa Networks party to any material litigation, pending or resolved in the last three years?
    Material litigation can affect a supplier's finances and continuity.
  8. Has Versa Networks lost any major customer or service-provider partner in the last two years, and why?
    Loss of major customers can indicate product or service problems.
  9. Have any senior executives left Versa Networks in the last two years, or been subject to adverse findings?
    Leadership instability affects delivery and support.
  10. What is the pricing basis and list price for VersaONE, for the hosted service and for customer-operated deployments?
    Without a pricing basis a bank cannot estimate cost at enterprise scale.
